questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Relevant courses at the university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most information was sent to us per mail by the university

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were divided into groups depending on our studies and if we were undergraduate or postgraduate. We were then given the contact info of our mentors that we could contact if we needed help at any point of our study.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: All throughout the intro week there were plenty of events where they gave us info on how things worked and where you should go if you needed further help with specific things.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms. Either your own dorm room with your own bathroom, or a shared dorm (up to 4 people) where you had your own room and shared common spaces and bathroom with the others.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were plenty of canteens with afordable options. There were also plenty of resturants on campus varying in price range. Only the dorm where you had your own room had a common kitchen for everyone to use and the shared dorm had space for you to have your own cooking appliences.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Each dorm offers cleaning 1-2 times a month, so students don't have to buy their own cleaning products.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After you are accepted you get a login to the page where you need to register for your courses. You need to know what level of courses you are allowed to take beforehand. After you've choosen your courses you lock them in and after that you can't change them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure as I didn't use it or search for it. However, I think there was a link to an email address where you could get help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of my courses without any problems.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you read everything about the course as the exam style is also written in the information about the course. This might help future students in choosing their courses more efficiently and help prevent exam stress if they now the exam style (either sit in or paper/essay).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the teachers were very black and white in what they were saying, which could become frustrating.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took level 4 courses which were the highest level. Level 1-3 were only for undergraduates unless it was a language course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching felt similar as it was a mix of lectures and seminars.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Current Issues in International Communications
Cross-cultural Management
Contemporary Security: States and People

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend "Current Issues in International Communications" and "Contemporary Security: States and People". I learned a lot in both of these couses while also using my own knowledge from past courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You pay for your own electricity and water.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Electricity was less expensive than I expected. Nothing was more expensive than I expected as I've studied in China before so I know the price range for most things.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are a bunch of clubs, but they many mainly operate in chinese. The club range from sports like basektball and rugby, to clubs about video games and movies. 
The sports center offers many sport classes that you can sign up for with no cost (unless you don't show up).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sports classes like arcery and sports classes you sign up for for the entire semester (there if sometimes a deposit you will get back if you don't have to much ansence). I did fencing for the entire semester and I loved it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around to the nearby citites. You can get to most of them by the high speed train and most of the tickets are cheap.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy as I've been on exchange to China before. However, if I haden't, the university does a lot for foreign students to get used to being there by doing events where you can experience different cultural things.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be shy and try to interact with them. Majority speaks english well enough to hold a conversation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes the chinese students lacked respect during the lectures and would speak loudly when the professor was teaching.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openess to foreigners and their focus on cleanliness in Ningbo.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Be open toward new experiences.
2: Try to get out and experience the surrounding areas or cities and don't just stay on campus. 
3: Don't be afraid of using the help provided for you while there (they offer consuling if you need it).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I made along the way. I made friends from all over the world by trying new things and being open.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes feeling lonely and homesick.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
